title: Anomalous suppression of quantum chaos between two integrable limits
authors: Roopayan Ghosh, Henry Davenport, Frank Schindler
abstract: Level statistics in non-integrable quantum many-body systems with time reversal symmetry are expected to follow the Gaussian Orthogonal Ensemble (GOE), a hallmark of quantum chaos. However, we show that the interacting Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model exhibits a clear suppression of the mean level-spacing ratio $\langle r\rangle$ from the GOE value $\approx 0.535$, persisting deep in the nonintegrable regime. This challenges the conventional association between non-integrability and fully chaotic spectral statistics. Using exact diagonalization supported by semi-analytical arguments, we trace this anomaly to incomplete hybridization of many-body band states inherited from the noninteracting band structure. The resulting restructuring of the spectrum weakens level repulsion without restoring integrability. We show the robustness of this mechanism in extensions of the model which break chiral and inversion symmetry.
summary: The paper reveals an unexpected suppression of quantum chaos ($\langle r angle$) in the interacting SSH model deep within the non-integrable regime. This effect is fundamentally linked to incomplete hybridization between many-body band states rather than simple spectral overlap or localization. The findings challenge conventional assumptions linking non-integrability directly to fully chaotic level statistics.
main_problem: The study investigates an anomalous suppression of quantum chaos, evidenced by reduced level repulsion ($\langle r angle$), in non-integrable many-body systems.
main_result: This anomaly is attributed not to integrability or disorder, but specifically to incomplete hybridization between distinct many-body band states inherited from the underlying single-particle structure.
method: The authors use exact diagonalization and semi-analytical perturbation theory to calculate level statistics ($\langle r angle$) across varying interaction strengths and hopping parameters.
model_or_system: The system is the interacting Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) chain model, described by a Hamiltonian combining non-interacting SSH terms with nearest-neighbor density-density interactions. The analysis probes transitions between integrable limits.
key_observables: Mean level-spacing ratio ($\langle r angle$), Inverse Participation Ratio (IPR), and the fluctuation measure $\Delta Q$ quantifying hybridization strength.
important_parameters: Alternating hopping parameter ($\delta$), interaction strength ($V_{	ext{int}}$), and symmetry breaking terms like staggered potential ($h$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on resolving symmetries to benchmark against GOE statistics, and the mechanism is linked to the geometry of many-body minibands.
figures_summary: Figures show $\langle r angle$ dipping anomalously in non-integrable regimes compared to GOE expectations; other figures map out the closing of MB band gaps and the correlation between minimal $\langle r angle$ and maximal hybridization fluctuations ($\Delta Q$).
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the system by first establishing the expected chaotic behavior (GOE), then identifying the anomalous dip in $\langle r angle$, attributing it to incomplete hybridization, and finally using advanced techniques like perturbation theory and symmetry analysis to quantify this geometric origin.
why_interesting: This work provides a detailed mechanism for spectral statistics deviations that are purely structural (band geometry) rather than arising from standard sources like disorder or integrability breaking, which is highly relevant for understanding quantum dynamics in engineered lattices.
